small_guidance:
- The conv (Conv2d 8→32, k=3, 128×256×256) dominates runtime; the fused post-conv kernel is already fast. Add an autotune config with BLOCK=8192/num_warps=8 and BLOCK=16384/num_warps=8 since HW=64516 is large — fewer chunks and bigger vector loads should reduce loop overhead.
- Replace the `tl.static_range(0, CPG_C)` two-pass loops with a true 2D load of shape `[CPG_C, BLOCK]` per chunk so each chunk computes sigmoid + accumulates sum/sumsq across all 4 channels at once; this halves the index math and lets Triton fuse the reductions better.
- Drop `num_stages=3` config (no benefit when the kernel is already memory-bound) and add a `num_stages=2, num_warps=8, BLOCK=2048` variant keyed on HW only.
large_guidance:
- The post-conv fused kernel is at ~99% of baseline already; the remaining headroom lives in nn.Conv2d. Replace the conv with a custom Triton implicit-GEMM kernel: one program per (N, OC-tile, output-spatial tile), GEMM-K = IC*kh*kw = 72, BLOCK_M (OC) = 32, BLOCK_N (spatial) = 128, BLOCK_K = 72 unrolled — and fuse bias-add, scale, sigmoid, *and* the GroupNorm first-pass reduction into the conv epilogue so the conv output never has to be re-read.
- Use channels_last (NHWC) layout end-to-end so the K loop over (IC,kh,kw) reads contiguous IC vectors; with IC=8 the K dim packs into a single 8-wide load per (kh,kw).
- Structure as a two-kernel design: (1) conv+bias+scale+sigmoid that also writes per-(N,group) partial sum/sumsq via atomics or a workspace; (2) a normalize/affine pass that reads the sigmoid output and applies (x-mean)*rstd*w+b. This eliminates the current kernel's redundant double sigmoid evaluation in the second pass.
